name: Independent Vowel AYANNA
description: Basic independent vowel Ayanna (U+0D85). Represents syllable-initial /a/.
purpose: Verify single code-point independent vowel rendering, cursor movement, and deletion.
expectedBehavior: Renders as a standalone vowel glyph. Selection and cursor jump across it in 1 step. 1 UTF-16 unit, 1 code point, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Load into text input. Press Right Arrow then Left Arrow. Press Backspace. Confirm clean deletion without leftover marks.
notes: Fundamental baseline independent vowel.

name: Independent Vowel AAYANNA
purpose: Verify that independent long vowel is treated as an indivisible unit.
expectedBehavior: Single glyph rendered. 1 UTF-16 unit, 1 code point, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Type after other text. Ensure caret does not position between glyph elements.
notes: Unlike consonant + aela-pilla, independent Aayanna is an atomic code point.

name: Independent Vowel IIYANNA
purpose: Check rendering and font metrics for upper loop structure.
expectedBehavior: No vertical clipping of the upper loop. 1 code point, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Check in input field and textarea. Verify upper loop does not clip against top border.
notes: Known font clipping risk in tight line-height containers.

name: Independent Vowel AUYANNA
purpose: Verify atomic treatment of two-part visual independent vowel.
expectedBehavior: Single atomic code point U+0D96. Must not be decomposed into Ayanna + Gayanukitta.
testInstructions: Inspect code points in Module B. Confirm U+0D96.
notes: Should not be confused with O-sign combinations.

name: Consonant + Aela-pilla (A-vowel)
description: Alpapraana Kayanna (U+0D9A) followed by Sinhala Vowel Sign Aela-pilla (U+0DCF).
purpose: Test standard post-base dependent vowel sign binding.
expectedBehavior: Rendered as a single visual syllable 'Kaa'. 2 UTF-16 units, 2 code points, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Place cursor after 'කා'. Press Backspace once. Observe whether entire cluster deletes or only aela-pilla is removed.
notes: Browser backspace behavior often differs: some delete the vowel sign (leaving 'ක'), others delete the entire cluster.

name: Consonant + Is-pilla (I-vowel)
purpose: Test above-base vowel sign rendering and vertical metrics.
expectedBehavior: Is-pilla rests cleanly on top of Kayanna without horizontal offset or top clipping.
testInstructions: Observe font rendering at 14px, 16px, and 24px. Check for vertical clipping.
notes: Commonly clipped in fixed line-height tables.

name: Consonant + Paa-pilla (U-vowel)
purpose: Test below-base vowel sign attachment.
expectedBehavior: Paa-pilla curves underneath base Kayanna. Must not collide with baseline or underline.
testInstructions: Underline the text in contenteditable or CSS. Verify underline does not strike through Paa-pilla.
notes: Below-base combining mark.

name: Consonant + Kombuva (E-vowel)
purpose: Test pre-base glyph reordering in logical vs visual display.
expectedBehavior: Visually, Kombuva displays to the LEFT of Kayanna, though stored logically AFTER Kayanna in memory (U+0D9A U+0DD9).
testInstructions: Check cursor navigation. Caret moving from left to right should logically select Kombuva then base, or treat whole cluster as 1 step.
notes: Logical order is Consonant + Vowel Sign. Visual rendering reorders Kombuva to the left.

name: Two-Part Vowel Sign Kombuva haa Aela-pilla (O-vowel)
purpose: Test circumfix vowel sign where parts surround the consonant on left and right.
expectedBehavior: Kombuva on left, Kayanna in middle, Aela-pilla on right. 2 code points (U+0D9A U+0DDC) in canonical NFC.
testInstructions: Inspect in Unicode Inspector and Normalization module. Compare with decomposed U+0D9A U+0DD9 U+0DCF.
notes: Canonical decomposition maps U+0DDC to U+0DD9 + U+0DCF.

name: Pure Consonant with Al-lakuna (Virama)
purpose: Verify suppression of inherent vowel and pure consonant flag rendering.
expectedBehavior: Renders with flag/hal mark over the right of Kayanna. 2 UTF-16 units, 2 code points, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Type in input. Backspace once. Verify if mark disappears or entire letter is deleted.
notes: Critical building block for conjuncts.

name: Yansaya on Kayanna
purpose: Verify medial Ya ligature formation via ZWJ.
expectedBehavior: Renders as single ligature glyph with sickle-like Yansaya tail curving below and to the right.
testInstructions: Confirm in text input and contenteditable. Cursor should treat the 4 code-point cluster as 1 grapheme unit.
notes: Missing ZWJ causes fallback to pure consonant followed by normal Ya ('ක්ය').

name: Yansaya on Tayanna
purpose: Verify dental Tayanna Yansaya formation in words like 'සත්‍ය' (truth).
expectedBehavior: Single combined glyph with Yansaya hook attached to Tayanna.
testInstructions: Select with mouse or Shift+Arrow. Ensure entire conjunct is selected as an atomic cluster.
notes: Essential word building block.

name: Rakaransaya on Kayanna
purpose: Verify medial Ra stroke formation under base consonant.
expectedBehavior: Renders as Kayanna with a lower hook/arch stroke representing medial -r- ('Kra').
testInstructions: Type in text input. Backspace once. Observe if Rakaransaya devolves to 'ක්ර' or deletes completely.
notes: Essential for loan words and Sanskrit/Pali derived terms (e.g. ක්‍රමය).

name: Rakaransaya on Payanna
purpose: Verify Rakaransaya ligature under open-top consonant Payanna (e.g. ප්‍රශ්නය).
expectedBehavior: Single conjunct glyph with lower stroke.
testInstructions: Copy to clipboard and paste back. Verify U+200D is preserved through clipboard round-trip.
notes: Clipboard bug risk: some systems strip ZWJ on paste, causing 'ප්ර'.

name: Complex Sacred Word SRI (ශ්‍රී)
description: Sayanna (U+0DC1) + Virama (U+0DCA) + ZWJ (U+200D) + Rayanna (U+0DBB) + Diga Is-pilla (U+0DD3).
purpose: Verify 5-code-point multi-modifier combining cluster (Sayanna + Rakaransaya + Long I vowel).
expectedBehavior: Single visual glyph in font rendering. Under UAX #29 grapheme segmentation, splits into 2 grapheme clusters (ශ්‍ and රී). 5 code points, 5 UTF-16 units, 15 UTF-8 bytes.
testInstructions: Measure in Length test module. Note the distinction between visual rendering (1 glyph) and UAX #29 grapheme clusters (2 clusters).
notes: Illustrates the fundamental divergence between OpenType glyph shaping and Unicode UAX #29 grapheme boundaries.

name: Repaya on Yayanna
purpose: Verify initial Ra ligature (Repaya / Reph) rendering over subsequent consonant.
expectedBehavior: Reph mark rendered as upper curl or joined form above/before consonant.
testInstructions: Observe rendering across different fonts. Compare Noto Sans Sinhala and Iskoola Pota.
notes: Rare in modern Sinhala, common in classical and religious Sinhala texts.

name: Bandi-akuru KSSHA (ක්ෂ)
purpose: Verify classic Sinhala conjunct ligature Kssha (as in ක්ෂේත්‍රය).
expectedBehavior: Fused ligature glyph. 4 code points, 4 UTF-16 units, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Test arrow key navigation. Caret should not stop inside the conjunct in modern browsers.
notes: Often mistakenly classified as a separate letter in traditional alphabets.

name: Bandi-akuru NNDA (ණ්ඩ)
purpose: Verify retroflex nasal conjunct ligature (as in මණ්ඩලය).
expectedBehavior: Touching or fused conjunct glyph where Nna merges into Dda without visible hal-lakuna flag.
testInstructions: Compare rendering with touch-consonant variant (using ZWNJ instead of ZWJ).
notes: Touching consonant behavior.

name: Bandi-akuru TTHA (ත්ත)
purpose: Verify geminate dental stop conjunct ligature (as in වෘත්තය).
expectedBehavior: Stacked or fused double Tayanna glyph without top hal-flag on first Tayanna.
testInstructions: Enter in textarea. Check word selection with double click.
notes: Very frequent in written Sinhala.

name: Sanyaka Gayanna (ඟ) vs Nasal Sequence (න්ග)
description: Single code-point prenasalized velar consonant Sanyaka Gayanna (U+0D9F).
purpose: Verify atomic prenasalized stop representation vs separate nasal + virama + consonant sequence.
expectedBehavior: Single atomic code point U+0D9F. Must NOT equal න්ග (U+0DB1 U+0DCA U+0D9C).
testInstructions: Compare 'ඟ' and 'න්ග' in Normalization module. Confirm they are neither canonically nor compatibility equivalent.
notes: Crucial linguistic distinction: Sanyaka consonants have distinct phonetic half-nasal timing.

name: Sanyaka Dayanna (ඳ) vs Nasal Sequence (න්ද)
purpose: Test contrast with nasal conjunct න්ද (U+0DB1 U+0DCA U+200D U+0DAF).
expectedBehavior: Single code point U+0DB3. 1 UTF-16 unit, 1 grapheme cluster.
testInstructions: Inspect in Unicode Inspector. Verify category is Consonant (Prenasalized).
notes: E.g. හඳ (moon) vs හන්දිය (junction).

name: Sinhala Archaic Punctuation Kunddaliya
purpose: Verify traditional full stop / sentence conclusion glyph rendering.
expectedBehavior: Decorative flourish glyph rendered without corrupting line heights or font fallback.
testInstructions: Place at end of a sentence. Verify word break boundaries in Intl.Segmenter.
notes: Historical punctuation, sometimes used stylistically in modern titles.

name: Sinhala Anusvaraya and Visargaya
purpose: Test combining nasal dot (Binduva / Anusvara) and visarga dots.
expectedBehavior: Binduva sits next to or slightly above base letter; visarga sits to the right.
testInstructions: Observe cursor travel between the signs.
notes: Binduva is frequently used in modern text (e.g. සිංහල).

name: Mixed Sinhala and English Sentence
testString: SiWIT යනු Web Interoperability පරීක්ෂා කිරීම සඳහා නිපදවූ Toolkit එකකි.
description: Bilingual sentence combining English technical terms and Sinhala case-marked grammar.
purpose: Verify inline font switching, line height consistency, and whitespace behavior across mixed Latin and Sinhala scripts.
expectedBehavior: No vertical line jitter between Latin and Sinhala words. Baseline alignments remain harmonious.
testInstructions: Paste into textarea and resize container width to test word-wrapping behavior.
notes: Line wrapping in browsers often fails on Sinhala word boundaries if zero-width spaces are absent.

name: Mixed Sinhala Currency and Numbers
description: Sri Lankan Rupee currency abbreviation with punctuated numeric amount and Sinhala genitive suffix.
purpose: Test punctuation, comma grouping, decimal dots, and Sinhala case suffixes on numbers.
expectedBehavior: Numeric grouping preserved, suffix attached smoothly.
testInstructions: Test selection and double click word boundaries around 'රු.' and numbers.
notes: Common in local finance web applications.

name: Canonical Decomposition of O-Vowel (කො)
description: Composed form (U+0D9A U+0DDC) vs decomposed form (U+0D9A U+0DD9 U+0DCF).
purpose: Test whether browser normalization canonicalizes decomposed kombuva + aela-pilla into atomic o-vowel sign.
expectedBehavior: Under NFC: normalizes to U+0D9A U+0DDC. Under NFD: decomposes to U+0D9A U+0DD9 U+0DCF. Visually identical on screen.
testInstructions: Load into Normalization module. Click 'Run Normalization Comparison'. Check byte diffs and equality flags.
sourceOrReference: Unicode Standard Annex #15 Unicode Normalization Forms
notes: Classic pitfall in Sinhala string search and database indexing.

name: ZWJ Stability under Normalization Forms
description: Word containing Rakaransaya with ZWJ (U+0D9A U+0DCA U+200D U+0DBB U+0DB8 U+0DBA).
purpose: Verify that NFC, NFD, NFKC, and NFKD do NOT strip or displace the ZWJ.
expectedBehavior: ZWJ (U+200D) is preserved in all four normalization forms because it is essential for script orthography.
testInstructions: Check code points after NFKC normalization. Confirm U+200D is retained.
notes: If a normalization pipeline incorrectly stripped ZWJ, 'ක්‍රමය' would corrupt into 'ක්රමය'.

name: Multi-Cluster Compound Word Truncation
description: Sinhala word for 'University' containing conjunct 'ශ්ව' and yansaya 'ද්‍ය'.
purpose: Examine disparity between UTF-16 length, code point count, and grapheme cluster count.
expectedBehavior: UTF-16 length is 14; code points count is 14; grapheme cluster count is 8; UTF-8 bytes is 42.
testInstructions: Input into Length module. Set maxlength to 8. Observe how the word is truncated and whether broken conjuncts occur.
notes: Shows that a naive maxlength in HTML cuts the word mid-character.

name: SRI LANKA Sacred Country Name
description: Country name containing complex multi-modifier cluster 'ශ්‍රී' and anusvara 'ලං'.
purpose: Evaluate input character counting and form validation rules.
expectedBehavior: Visual syllables: 4. Code points: 10. UTF-16: 10. Grapheme clusters: 5 (including space).
testInstructions: Test in input field with maxlength 5 vs 10.
sourceOrReference: Common Form Validation Cases in Sri Lanka
notes: Demonstrates why character count rules in government/banking portals often miscount.
